note: v3, bars 25-26 (1:27.3–1:34.5): the sharp reed glides from the width of five to the width of seven and the band, which plays the pair's pulse, accelerates with it (twelve pulses where there were ten). Snare and china keep the bar. The key changes at 1:34.5 and the pulse does not.

chirper-zero v11: the ending. The band holds the last chord one bar and lets go at the bar line (3:27.3); the two reeds are alone, in tune and still, for the last bar. The band is on the reeds note (strings tuned, fifths 3:2). The lead no longer cancels the reeds second overtone (its oscillator starts half a cycle on).

v14 (chirper-one): the handpan comes back inside the band in 'square again' and names the pair's fifth overtone: A5, five stopped strokes to the pulse, from 2:40.0 on one pulse a bar, from 2:47.3 on two, from 2:54.5 (the next window) on every pulse, to 3:01.8. 70 strokes on a new track; nothing else changed.
v15 (chirper-alpha): bar 39, 2:18.2-2:21.8: the pair is stopped a fourth higher with the peg left alone, so everything in the rule is a fourth up and four to the bar for one bar of 'three'

v18, the string gives: in the third and fourth bars of square (0:43.6-0:50.9) the hair narrows to half a pulse a beat and is pulled back; the band follows the pair down and up under a snare and china that keep time, and the lead comes with it
v20: the band leaves every fourth pulse of five to the pair (bars 20-24, 1:12.0-1:24.4): five one-pulse rests that walk back through the bar, the reeds alone in them; 75 strokes out, nothing added
v22: the first two bars rewritten (0:00-0:07.3): the second reed comes in two pulses a beat sharp and is tuned down to the first; eight slowing swells, the eighth on the first drum stroke

v24: 3:20.0-3:22.1, between the band's last stroke and the last chord: the handpan names overtones 3 to 15 of the pair, each as it swells for the last time (thirteen notes, the gaps closing), and the finger cymbals ring the sixteenth, their own note; then 1.5 s of stillness and the chord

v26 (chirper-zero): seven sevens. 1:45.5-2:03.6 (on into w5 through the turn of the peg): the drummer feet roll the pair seventh overtone between the kicks, 49 to the bar, three bars; then the roll slows with the peg into three. One new track, feet.

v28 (chirper-zero): the band still counts three: in bars 44-47 (2:39.1-2:48.2) the band leaves every third pulse of four to the two reeds, a place earlier each bar; the last rest, on the downbeat, is the handpans five alone with the pair. 72 strokes out, nothing added. Answers v20.

v29, the pair plays a tune: in three the two reeds climb the low A flat string harmonics a bar at a time with the peg left alone (A flat four at 2:14.5, C five at 2:18.2, the seventh seven at 2:21.8) and the band climbs and quickens with them; chirper-alpha plan from v15, his bar a bar earlier
